posts.topic: Pressing as you sew: press don't iron, press every seam, use a pressing cloth

slides.title: Press as you sew: 3 habits that change everything
slides.subtitle: The difference between homemade and handmade is often the iron. Here's how to use it like a pro.

slides.title: Press, don't iron
slides.body: Lift the iron and set it down on the fabric instead of sliding it back and forth. Sliding can stretch curves and pull seams out of shape.

slides.title: Press every seam
slides.body: Press each seam flat as sewn to set the stitches, then press it open or to one side. Do it before you cross it with another seam.

slides.title: Use a pressing cloth
slides.body: Lay a piece of cotton between the iron and your fabric. It stops shiny marks on wool, dark colours and delicate fabrics.

slides.title: Save this for sewing day
slides.body: Our step-by-step instructions tell you exactly when to press, so every seam looks crisp.

posts.caption_ig:
Want your makes to look less homemade and more handmade? Keep the iron next to your machine 🪡

Swipe for 3 pressing habits: press instead of ironing, press every seam before crossing it, and use a pressing cloth on delicate fabrics.

It feels slower at first, but it saves so much fiddling later ✨

posts.topic: Test fusible interfacing on a scrap of your fabric first

slides.title: Test your interfacing on a scrap first
slides.body: Fuse a small piece of interfacing to a fabric offcut before you start. Check it bends like your fabric, with no bubbles or stiffness. Too heavy? Choose a lighter weight.

posts.caption_ig:
Collars that feel like cardboard? Facings full of bubbles? Blame the interfacing, not yourself 🧵

Before you fuse it to your real pieces, test it on a scrap of the same fabric. It should bend and drape like the fabric, just with a little more body.

Too stiff? Go a weight lighter. Bubbling? Use a pressing cloth, more steam and hold the iron still for longer ✨

Do you test first, or fuse and hope? 😅

#sewingtips #fabric #sewingforbeginners #sewinghacks #isew
posts.caption_fb:
Quick fabric tip: always test your interfacing on a scrap first 🧵

Fuse a small piece to an offcut of your fabric and check how it feels. It should add support without turning stiff or bubbly. If it's too heavy, switch to a lighter weight before you fuse your real pieces.

posts.topic: Taking in or letting out the waist at the side seams

slides.title: Waist too loose or too tight?
slides.subtitle: Your XS–XL size fits everywhere else? Fix the waist at the side seams in three easy steps.

slides.title: Measure the difference
slides.body: Try the garment on inside out. Pin out the extra at the waist, or note how much you need to add, then measure that amount.

slides.title: Share it between seams
slides.body: Divide the total by four, one for each side seam edge. Small amounts spread evenly sit much better than one big change.

slides.title: Blend back smoothly
slides.body: Redraw the side seam with a gentle curve that returns to the original line above and below the waist. No sharp corners.

slides.title: Find your perfect fit
slides.body: Every pattern includes sizes XS–XL with US and UK sizing and a clear size chart.

posts.caption_ig:
Your size fits perfectly at the bust and hip, but the waist has other ideas? Totally normal 📏

Bodies don't follow size charts exactly, so a small waist tweak is one of the most common adjustments.

Swipe for 3 steps: measure the difference, share it between the side seams, then blend back to the original line.
